claude.sample_unit: patients with iron deficiency anemia undergoing GI endoscopy

links.outcome: Local validation of UK-developed IDIOM model discrimination and calibration on local retrospective data
links.effect: AuROC 62.9% (95% CI 56.8-68.9) vs 69.7-77.1% in UK cohorts; calibration slope 0.27, CITL 3.47, indicating poor local calibration and underestimated risk.
links.quote: The model demonstrated lower performance in our Thai cohort compared to the original UK cohorts (AuROC 62.9% vs. 69.7%–77.1%).

links.outcome: Comparison of development and local populations to explain performance differences
links.effect: GI malignancy prevalence was 21.3% vs 7.6-8.4% in UK datasets; median age 63 vs 69-74; different IDA criteria; these differences likely explain the risk underestimation.
links.quote: This disparity may be largely attributed to the higher prevalence of GI malignancy observed in our cohort (21.3% vs. 7.6%–8.4% in the original dataset) [ 15 ].

links.outcome: Effect of recalibration and refitting on local model calibration and discrimination
links.effect: Recalibration fixed CITL (3.465 to 0.000) and slope (0.272 to 1.000) with unchanged AuROC; refitting raised AuROC from 62.87% to 67.23%, only marginal discrimination improvement.
links.quote: However, despite these adjustments, the discrimination ability showed only marginal improvement in the AuROC.

links.outcome: Generalization of a UK-developed predictive model to a new population
links.effect: IDIOM showed AuROC 62.9% in Thai patients with extreme risk underestimation (CITL 3.47, slope 0.27); very-low-risk group still had 18.1% GI malignancy prevalence.
links.quote: Moreover, the calibration of the model in our cohort showed an extreme underestimation of the risk.

links.outcome: Recalibration of model after population change to correct miscalibration
links.effect: Recalibration-in-the-large brought CITL from 3.465 to 0.000; logistic recalibration adjusted calibration slope from 0.272 to 1.000.
links.quote: Initially, recalibration‐in‐the‐large adjusted the CITL in the validation study from 3.465 to 0.000, while the calibration slope and AuROC remained unchanged.

links.quote: In addition, the calibration parameters also indicated a poorly calibrated model [calibration slope of 0.27 (95% CI 0.14–0.40) and CITL of 3.47 (95% CI 3.20–3.73)] (Table 3 ) [ 23 ].

links.effect: Thai AuROC 62.9% versus original UK cohorts 69.7%–77.1%.
links.quote: The model demonstrated lower performance in our Thai cohort compared to the original UK cohorts (AuROC 62.9% vs. 69.7%–77.1%).

links.effect: CITL improved 3.465 to 0.000 and slope 0.272 to 1.000; refitted AuROC increased 62.87% to 67.23%.
links.quote: However, despite these adjustments, the discrimination ability showed only marginal improvement in the AuROC.

links.effect: AuROC 78.57% in thalassemia vs 61.43% nonthalassemia; CITL 2.674 vs 3.514.
links.quote: Discrimination and calibration performance were higher in the thalassemia group than in the nonthalassemia group (Table 5 ).

links.effect: Very-low-risk group still had 18.1% GI malignancy prevalence.
links.quote: However, even in the very low‐risk group, the prevalence of GI malignancy remained high at 18.1% (Table S3 ).

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of IDIOM model in Thai cohort
links.effect: AuROC was 62.9% (95% CI 56.8–68.9%), CITL was 3.47 (95% CI 3.20–3.73), and calibration slope was 0.27 (95% CI 0.14–0.40), underestimating risk.
links.quote: The external discriminative performance of the updated IDIOM model in the Chiang Mai dataset was only fair (AuROC 62.9%, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 56.8–68.9) and the AuROC values were also lower than those found in previous external validations (Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Model discrimination and calibration after recalibration and refitting
links.effect: Refitting improved AuROC to 67.23% (95% CI 61.13–73.34%), CITL to 0.000 (95% CI -0.228 to 0.228), and calibration slope to 1.000 (95% CI 0.637–1.363).
links.quote: The refitted model showed an AuROC of 67.23%, a CITL of 0.000, and a calibration slope of 1.000.

screen.practice: local validation and recalibration before deployment
screen.reason: The study validates and recalibrates the IDIOM model, which is a simple statistical risk score / logistic regression model based on 4 clinical parameters (age, sex, Hb, MCV), not an advanced AI or machine learning system of interest, and lacks health care deployment/safeguard evaluation.
